answer: Every participant locks a bond and receives one unlinkable credential per epoch after a random human-verification check. Three audit pools—named inlet, cedar, and relic—cross-check duplicate device proofs and publish signed fraud evidence. Reusing a credential or coordinating conflicting actions invalidates every linked claim and slashes the bonds after an appeal window. A Sybil attacker therefore must finance and independently verify each alias, so scaling identities becomes expensive.
